div.h2: Hiring is looked after by the hiring team
div.p: This is where every request for a new person lives — who asked, whether there is budget for it, who agreed it, and how the candidates are getting on. If you run a part of the business you can raise a request here; ask your HR administrator to put your name against your department and this screen fills in.
Every request for a new person, from the moment somebody asks to the moment the advert goes out.

button.title: Chase the adverts nobody has agreed and the roles nobody is recruiting — exactly what the nightly step does

div.b: Nobody has been named as a recruiter yet
div.p: A hiring rule says, per company and country, who picks a request up once it has been agreed and who their manager is. Without one a role is still agreed perfectly well — it just sits with nobody recruiting it, and Payobook chases the hiring administrators about it every day. It is one line to write.

input.placeholder: Search a role, a department, a recruiter…

div.p: Whoever runs a part of the business raises the first one. It goes to their manager, then to the HR lead — and to Finance as well, but only if it asks for more than the budget has left. Once everybody has agreed, the role gets a job, a recruiter and a page every employee can refer somebody on.

div.p: Open a role on the Roles tab, find the candidate you want to meet and press Arrange. Everybody gets an invitation with a calendar file in it, Payobook reminds them the day before and again half an hour before, and afterwards each person on the panel gets their own private link to say what they thought.
